deepdive.sec: Integrated Power Utility & Solar Manufacturing (Gen-T&D + RE EPC/IPP + Cell/Module mfg)

bull_bear.body:
- Disciplined growth: net debt/underlying EBITDA 3.3x, net debt/equity 1.2x maintained as guardrails.
- Self-funding via strong subsidiary cash generation; backward integration (wafer/ingot) to capture more value chain.
- Coal asset sale as potential deleveraging/value-crystallization optionality.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- Transmission/ROW & TBCB/ISTS evacuation delays — primary cause of capex slippage; recurring risk.
- Solar curtailment / temporary-GNA risk on RE evacuation.
- Mundra: remaining 4 states' SPPA signing pending (regulatory approval risk); Section 11 interim.
- Indonesian coal export tax/royalty (under discussion) — mitigated by pass-through.
- Delhi regulatory true-ups are lumpy/unpredictable — FY27 reported numbers could be lower if fewer approvals; regulatory-asset wind-down dependence on regulator affidavit.
- Tata Projects return to profit not yet proven.
- Deferred-tax asset recognition flatters PAT (non-cash, one-off).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, measured, candid. CEO repeatedly stresses "calibrated growth" and balance-sheet discipline; acknowledged capex miss openly and attributed to deliberate caution on GNA. Strong transparency on subsidiary numbers; offered to improve disclosure quality. Tone constructive and credible, not promotional.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The capex "miss" is partly self-imposed discipline (refusing to strand assets on temporary GNA) — quality of growth, not weakness.
- DCR/domestic-cell mandate (1-Jun-2026 rooftop; 1-Sep-2025 utility tenders; 1-Jun-2028 wafers) structurally captures Tata Power's captive manufacturing — vertical integration becomes a regulatory moat.
- Future RE economics shift to hybrid+storage bundled deals with C&I/data centres — higher returns than the depressed pure-RE auction tariffs of FY24–25.
- Two PAT boosters this year (INR783 cr Delhi true-ups + INR250 cr deferred tax) are partly non-recurring — watch FY27 base.
- Nuclear SMR is a long-dated free option, not yet in numbers.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Deck frames the balance sheet as a "Comfortable Debt Position For Sustainable Growth"; Net Debt Rs 61,238 Cr in Q1 FY27 vs Rs 56,122 Cr in Q4 FY26 and Rs 47,578 Cr in Q1 FY26, with the increase attributed to higher capex and WC requirements.
- Net Debt to Equity 1.25 in Q1 FY27 (1.18 in FY26, 2.19 in FY19); Net Debt to Underlying EBITDA 3.41 in Q1 FY27 (3.34 in FY26, 5.19 in FY19), based on trailing twelve months.
- Credit ratings (Consolidated, current): CRISIL AA+/Stable, India Ratings AA+/Stable, ICRA AA+/Stable, CARE AA+/Stable, S&P Global BBB/Stable, Moody's Ba1/Positive — an upgrade path from AA/Stable and BB+/Stable in FY23.
- Total Gross Debt (LT + ST) of Rs 74,069 Cr at Q1 FY27, with RE Gencos the largest block at Rs 31,734 Cr and Tata Power Standalone at Rs 23,966 Cr; cash & cash equivalents Rs 12,831 Cr and networth Rs 49,026 Cr.
- Risk mitigation on the growth pipeline: land acquired/visibility for all under-construction RE projects, transmission connectivity secured, and 87% of pipeline RE projects tied in LT PPA.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Solar manufacturing**: stabilized, high yields, INR857 cr PAT (>2x). Captive cell/module to feed own IPP + rooftop; DCR mandate (effective 1-Jun-2026) a tailwind.
- **Odisha DISCOM**: standout, INR809 cr PAT; further loss-reduction runway.
- **Delhi (DDL)**: prior-period regulatory true-ups (INR783 cr FY26); regulatory asset to amortize over 6 yrs to 2032 (SC/APTEL monitored, affidavit given).
- **Mumbai (IEL/Mumbai Transmission)**: recurring ~INR1,000 cr/yr capex, RoE on 30% equity (70-30) — steady regulated growth.
- **Tata Projects**: legacy DFC/Barmer refinery projects nearly done; expected to return to profit FY27.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Presented as "India's largest vertically-integrated power company" across four pillars: Renewables, Transmission & Distribution, Generation and New-age Energy Solutions.
- Claims "India's #1 Solar Roof co. for 11 years running" in the rooftop solar business.
- Business is split in the deck between "Regulated businesses" and "Non-Regulated Businesses"; the EBITDA bridge shows growth driven by both.
- Q1 FY27 commentary states EBITDA grew 8% YoY "driven by growth across all three clusters excluding Mundra" (Generation & Coal, Renewables, T&D).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Regulatory/Mundra] The Mundra plant continues to run under Section 11 (vs SPPA earlier), and the EBITDA bridge shows Mundra, Coal and Shipping as a negative contributor; Scope 1 emissions and water consumption both fell due to "Mundra Shutdown".
- [Coal assets] Coal mines KPC, BSSR and AGM are held at Tata Power share of 26%, 26% and 30% respectively (production data on 100% basis); associate income from coal companies is a stated PAT driver.
- [Regulated base] Regulated Equity total of Rs 15,178 Cr and Regulated Assets total of Rs 10,790 Cr at Q1 FY27 (deck's own labels, Rs Crore).
- [Industry backdrop] Deck cites Rs 9.2 tn of transmission capex anticipated in India between FY25-32E (Inter-State Rs 6.6 tn, Intra-State Rs 2.7 tn), All India AT&C losses down to 15% in FY25, and India's power consumption per capita at 1,400 units.
- [Deck inconsistency] Bhutan hydro capacities differ between the map and the project table: the map labels Khorlochhu HPP 740 MW, Dorjilung HPP 600 MW and Gongri HPP 1,125 MW, while the table states Khorlochhu HPP 600, Dorjilung HPP 1,125 and Gongri HPP 740 (MW). Similarly the manufacturing plant is described as "~4.9 GW Integrated cell & module manufacturing capacity" on the overview slide but as "TP Solar (4.3 GW Cell & module Manufacturing Plant)" in the segment tables.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- EBITDA margin expansion driven by manufacturing, Odisha, rooftop.
- Mundra: coal cost is full pass-through (FOB incl. any Indonesian export duty/royalty) under SPPA — protects margin from coal/tax shocks.
- Indonesian coal prices expected ~flat (±5%); shipping/coal cost increases "nominal."
- Curtailment a drag on solar PLF (varies 20–80% evacuation by site); reimbursed where GNA in place.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- PAT INR1,416 cr (Q4) vs Q4FY25 INR1,306 cr (+8%); EBITDA INR4,216 cr vs INR3,829 cr (+10%).
- FY26 first-ever full-year PAT >INR5,000 cr; EBITDA INR16,090 cr (+11%).
- Mundra: moved from loss-drag (9 months non-operational) to operating under Section 11 with SPPA billing; Gujarat SPPA signed this period (prior quarters: unsigned).
- FY27 capex guidance reiterated at ~INR25,000 cr after FY26 came in light at INR13,000 cr (vs ~INR22–25k cr originally guided).
- Delhi regulatory true-up INR783 cr FY26 vs INR333 cr FY25 (Q4 component ~INR320 cr after Q3 ~INR460 cr).
- New deferred-tax asset INR250 cr recognized in Q4 (not in prior quarters).
- Nuclear SMR (2x220 MW), 10 GW wafer/ingot plant, and hybrid+C&I/data-center RE model freshly elaborated this call.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log

outlook.body:
- FY27 capex guidance: ~INR25,000 cr (deferred FY26 projects roll into FY27); FY28 expected similar (~INR25,000 cr).
- FY27 commissioning: ~2.5 GW total RE (solar+wind), of which solar ~1.5–1.8 GW; "everything is not solar" — heavily hybrid/FDRE.
- ~600 MW utility-scale to complete in current quarter (slipped from FY26).
- 5 GW in-house RE pipeline: ~50% complete in FY27, balance in FY28.
- Odisha: FY27 likely the peak performance year; AT&C losses to fall ~2%/yr toward 12–13% over 4–5 years.
- Mundra SPPA: Gujarat done; remaining 4 procurers expected signed in 4–6 weeks.
- Rooftop: target 50–60% growth FY27 (after 100% growth FY26); 20% market-share target over 3 years.
outlook.title: Guidance (next quarter / FY27)

outlook.body:
- Total RE pipeline ~5 GW (in-house), all hybrid/FDRE-weighted; pure solar in pipeline small (~600 MW).
- Operational capacity 16.7 GW → 26.3 GW incl. pipeline (~10 GW addition), spread across FY30–FY32.
- Pumped-hydro: 2,800 MW Shirwata (work starts FY26); Bhivpuri pumped-hydro.
- Bhutan hydro: 600 MW + 1,125 MW (1,125 MW commissions ~2031–32); World Bank financing tied up.
- Wind turbines for hybrid projects already tied up.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Hybrid/FDRE + storage**: new model — RE bundled with pumped-hydro for utilities AND C&I (Tata Steel, data centres) at superior returns vs pure solar/wind bids of last 2 yrs.
- **Nuclear (SMR)**: working with 3 state govts, land + water allocation identified, geotech studies + DPRs underway with NPCIL; 2x220 MW (440 MW) units; DPRs in ~6 months.
- **Wafer/ingot plant**: new 10 GW plant in 2 phases (backward integration; Indian wafers needed from 1-Jun-2028).
- **Coal monetization**: Indonesian coal assets could be sold post full SPPA signing if valuation attractive (optional, premature).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Tata Power is delivering a calibrated, balance-sheet-disciplined growth story — Mundra's loss-drag is resolved via supplementary PPA, solar cell/module manufacturing and Odisha DISCOM are compounding profits, and the next leg is vertically-integrated hybrid (FDRE) renewables backed by captive cell supply, pumped-hydro storage and optionality in nuclear.
